answer:
Password cracking primarily involves an adversary attempting to guess a password by trying every possible combination until they succeed. This method is known as a brute force attack. It is computationally feasible and guarantees success as it systematically goes through all potential passwords based on the character set used (including lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, and symbols) and the maximum length of the password [Source 1].

Adversaries may employ brute force techniques to access accounts when they do not know the passwords or when they have obtained password hashes. This process involves systematically guessing the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism [Source 2]. Brute forcing can occur at various stages during a breach, often leveraging information gathered from other activities within the compromised environment [Source 3].

## Attack description

An adversary tries every possible value for a password until they succeed. A brute force attack, if feasible computationally, will always be successful because it will essentially go through all possible passwords given the alphabet used (lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, symbols, etc.) and the maximum length of the password.
